sermon.title: Job’s Response to God 02/24/2019
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing the series on surviving tragedy, Pastor David G. Kincer looks at Job’s response when God spoke: five actions that lead to restoration from any tragedy. Say God is almighty, admit your error, see with spiritual eyes, repent of wrong behavior, and forgive and pray for your enemies, as Job did before God restored all he had.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Job 42:16 says Job lived 140 years after this; the caption reads “165 years” (34:46), kept as spoken. He starts to cite James 5:16 then corrects to Matthew 6:14.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the LORD restored Job’s losses when he prayed for his friends. Indeed the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been his acquaintances before, came to him and ate food with him in his house; and they consoled him and comforted him for all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. Each one gave him a piece of silver and each a ring of gold. Now the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; for he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys. He also had seven sons and three daughters.

faqs.question: What was Satan created for?
faqs.answer: He says to lie, accuse, tempt and destroy.

faqs.question: Must we speak our faith?
faqs.answer: Yes; silent saints don’t get much.

faqs.question: How did he avoid weird doctrines?
faqs.answer: Believe nothing until you confirm it in the Bible.

faqs.question: Does God want to destroy you?
faqs.answer: No, He wants to destroy the wrong behavior.

How long did Job’s trial last?
